_doc: Every number someone may want to turn. One row = one value. side = who uses it.
rows: the Palworld near plane (UE default, 10 cm)
a block must be this far behind a Palworld surface to be hidden
how strongly Palworld brightness lights blocks
how much of the Palworld light colour blocks take
time per tick spent answering terrain rays
rays answered even on a slow tick
how far above a downward ray's start to look for the surface of a hill it may be inside
Pals farther than this from Steve are not sent to Minecraft
Minecraft damage points that equal a full health bar
extra multiplier on Minecraft damage dealt to Pals
Minecraft is gone if its heartbeat stalls this long
HP loss below this fraction of max counts as a status tick, not a hit
a status tick only reaches Steve with a hostile this close; otherwise it is the hidden character's hunger or cold
largest layer Minecraft sends, in megapixels (2560x1440 fits)
below this for two seconds, Minecraft sends the next smaller layer size
time for one dig with no fitting tool
a dug spot yields again after this long
a hit only reaches Steve with a hostile this close; otherwise the hidden character starves, freezes or fell, which is Palworld's survival and not Steve's
how far a fire or a block of ice reaches
how often Palworld takes Steve's food and reports temperature
after changing its heat source, the mod waits this long for Palworld's temperature to follow
narrowest hitbox half-width a Pal gets in Minecraft
lowest hitbox half-height a Pal gets in Minecraft
the PalCraft world is saved this often while both games run
Palworld mode: Steve is drawn with at least this much block light, so Palworld's night does not turn him into a silhouette
Palworld mode: with the camera closer to Steve than this (a wall behind it), Steve is not drawn
and he is drawn again once it is this far away
Palworld mode, swimming: Steve lies flat with the underside of his body this far above the middle of the character (negative: below it), which puts him half out of the water
Palworld mode: wait between searches for Palworld's player gauge while it is not on screen
Palworld mode: its gauges are told to stay faded this often, since Palworld animates them
the character's health is read this often for Minecraft's hearts, and Palworld is asked whether build mode is up
while the Palworld character is hidden, its tools are looked over this often, so a newly equipped one is hidden too
Melty test: Lua memory is judged after this many ticks with Minecraft linked and terrain answered
and passes under this much; the out-parameter leak of 0.2.0 reached it in 15 seconds
Palworld experience for a level 1 Pal that Steve kills
how fast that experience grows with the Pal's level: base * level ^ power
multiplier for an alpha or boss
Palworld mode: the camera sits this much further behind than Palworld's own, because Steve is wider than its character; a wall behind shortens it
Palworld mode: and this much further to the right, which keeps Steve left of the crosshair at the longer distance
Palworld's own shot (a conversation, a cutscene): Steve is drawn into it while Minecraft's frame was made within this distance of the shot's camera
and within this angle and field of view
a shot that keeps moving faster than that for this long shows Palworld's own character instead
a Pal counts as at most this many levels above the character, so an easy win over a strong Pal does not skip the early game
